$comment: CockroachDB Cloud Managed MCP Server — analyst access to Recall's memory.
Generated from the CockroachDB Cloud Console (cluster > Connect > Model
Context Protocol). Point any MCP-compatible client at it — Claude Code,
Cursor, VS Code — and an analyst can ask questions of the corpus, the
decisions and the actions in natural language, including historical ones,
because AS OF SYSTEM TIME works through it.
There is no secret in this file. mcp-cluster-id is the cluster's UUID, not
a credential; authentication happens separately, either through the OAuth
flow (interactive) or a service-account API key (autonomous).
SETUP
claude mcp add cockroachdb-cloud https://cockroachlabs.cloud/mcp \
--transport http \
--header "mcp-cluster-id: f0e1c1fc-ab2f-40c8-b25f-00c70d5c54a0"
claude /mcp        then choose cockroachdb-cloud > Authenticate
ACCESS
Read-only by default — the managed server does not write unless write
access is explicitly granted, and every call is audit-logged in the Cloud
Console.
For unattended use, authenticate with a service account rather than
OAuth. This project uses `recall-mcp-reader`, whose description is
literally 'Read-only MCP analyst access to Recall agent memory. No write
privileges.' Supply its API key as a Bearer token; keep it out of the
repo.
That gives two independent layers. The service account bounds what the
MCP server can reach at the CockroachDB Cloud level; the recall_reader
SQL user bounds what any connection can do inside the database, where
every write is refused with SQLSTATE 42501 (see create_reader.py
--verify). Neither depends on the other being configured correctly.
